en_excerpt_original: 「Should we buy bento or not?」 The moment we stepped into the convenience store, I started arguing with Sendai-san about it. I thought going home and cooking now was a hassle, while Sendai-san insisted we already had ingredients and that since it was New Year's Eve, we should eat something proper. Our opinions kept going nowhere, and in the end, we settled it with rock-paper-scissors—which Sendai-san won, so we went with what she wanted. 「This is such a pain. I think we should just eat whatever and laze around.」 I complained to Sendai-san, who had just dropped two cream puffs into the basket. 「It's the last day of the year, so let's eat something proper,」 she said, trying to make today feel meaningful. 「December thirty-first happens next year too, you know.」 I tossed two puddings into the basket. 「Does that mean you'll spend next year's New Year's Eve with me too, Miyagi?」 「It's not like I have anything else to do anyway.」 「Are you still holding a grudge about what I said earlier?」 「Not really.」 When Sendai-san had suggested watching the first sunrise, I'd told her, "I'd get sleepy, so no," and she'd replied, "It's not like you have anything else to do, right?" I wasn't bothered by it or anything. Maika wasn't around, and it was true that I had nothing else to do. But even if I did have plans, if Sendai-san wanted to spend next New Year's Eve the same way as today, I figured I wouldn't mind spending it with her. If I filled my calendar with plans involving her, I wouldn't have to deal with boring time spent alone, so it wasn't something I needed to strongly refuse. 「Sendai-san, this too.」 I added a chocolate bar to the basket. 「Is there anything else you want?」 「Ramune candy. What about you, Sendai-san?」 「Potato chips.」 We tossed snacks that didn't feel special at all into the basket, paid, and left the convenience store. We chatted about nothing in particular as we walked home, then started making mizutaki hot pot. 「Miyagi, get the clay pot out.」 Sendai-san called out, and my stomach—which should've still been full from the cheesecake—let out a loud growl in response, making her laugh. I kicked her in the leg as she peered into the fridge, then got the clay pot ready. Sendai-san cut up the ingredients, made the broth in the small clay pot, and added the chicken. She skimmed the foam while the chicken cooked through, then added the sliced vegetables, mushrooms, and tofu to simmer. After that, we carried the pot and rice over to Sendai-san's room. 「Why aren't we eating in the shared living space? Cleaning up is going to be a pain.」 I asked Sendai-san, who was setting chopsticks on the calico cat and black cat rests. 「It's New Year's Eve, so doing something different from usual makes it feel more special.」 「I think normal is fine.」 「Normal is fine too, but not-normal is also fine, right? Let's eat.」 Saying that, Sendai-san sat down with her back against the bed, and I sat across from her. Then, without either of us prompting the other, we said, "Let's eat," and picked up our chopsticks. I took some cabbage and chicken into my bowl with the ponzu sauce and stared at it. When was the last time I'd had hot pot? I tried digging through my memory, but I couldn't remember. 「Would you have preferred something other than mizutaki?」 I heard Sendai-san's voice and looked up. Until I started living with her, my meals had mostly been retort pouches, frozen food, or bento—I'd hardly ever cooked for myself, so there was no way I'd easily find a memory of eating hot pot. 「I've barely ever had hot pot before, so anything's fine.」 I quietly gave the answer I'd arrived at from my memories, then bit into the chicken, chewed it well, and swallowed. Hot pot eaten alone would be boring, so even if my past self had been someone who cooked, I probably wouldn't have made it. 「I see. Is it good?」 I answered, "It's good," to the girl who didn't ask why I never made hot pot, and she gave me a smile in return. Sendai-san was always kind. But I couldn't find anything to give back for the kindness she offered so unconditionally, and it made me feel a little uncomfortable. I dropped my gaze to the black cat chopstick rest and ate the cabbage and chicken. I took some mizuna greens and tofu into my bowl and looked at the penguin plush lying on the bed. It was the one I'd won for her from the crane game on Christmas, and it seemed to move around to different spots depending on the day. Sometimes it was on the floor, sometimes sitting on the bed. Today, it was tucked under the covers in Sendai-san's place, sleeping. I couldn't tell if she was taking good care of it or not. 「Sendai-san, you said you wanted a penguin plush, but do you actually like that one?」 I thought back to Sendai-san's birthday. She'd said she wanted to have the kind of ordinary conversation anyone could have, and she'd mentioned she'd started liking penguins and that she should've bought a plush. Though I wasn't sure if a plush won from a crane game counted. 「I like it. I use it as a body pillow.」 「Do you really like penguins that much?」 「You're the one who likes penguins, aren't you, Miyagi?」 Sendai-san replied with a question of her own, eating her tofu while complaining about how hot it was. 「I'm not talking about me. I'm asking if you like penguins.」 「I do. That's why I sleep with it.」 The penguin sleeping on the bed wasn't small enough to fit in the palm of my hand, but it wasn't big enough to make me want to hug it to sleep either. If she wanted a body pillow, I thought she should get something bigger. 「Isn't that penguin a little too small to use as a body pillow?」 「Then will you be my body pillow instead, Miyagi?」 「Of course I won't.」 I glared at Sendai-san for saying something so stupid and took another piece of chicken from the pot. Sendai-san took some chicken too and dipped it in ponzu. We kept talking about trivial things as we emptied the pot, but our pace was slower than usual, and the food didn't disappear quickly. I wasn't sure if our pointless conversation was lively or not, but eating hot pot at a leisurely pace was good, and I was glad we hadn't bought bento at the convenience store. 「Miyagi, which do you want? Pudding or cream puff?」 Once the pot was down to just broth, Sendai-san asked brightly from across the table. 「You can decide, Sendai-san.」 「Which do you like better, Miyagi?」 「Then, pudding.」 At times like this, Sendai-san almost never chose her own favorite. She always let me pick what I liked. That made me happy, but it also seemed like she was covering up her own feelings. Pudding or cream puff. Which one we ate first wasn't a big deal. But if she wanted to have the kind of ordinary conversation anyone could have, she should give her own opinion once in a while. It was something trivial, but when she kept too many things from me, it started to bother me. 「Okay, wait here a bit. I'll go grab them.」 Sendai-san, who still wouldn't tell me whether she actually wanted the pudding or the cream puff, stood up. She left the room and came back almost immediately, setting the puddings and spoons on the table. 「Was pudding what you wanted to eat, Sendai-san?」 「Yeah.」 Sendai-san, who had been the one to put the cream puffs in the basket at the convenience store, smiled as she peeled the lid off her pudding. Giving up on pressing further, I peeled my lid off too and took a bite of pudding. It was soft, cold, and delicious. I took another bite, and Sendai-san patted the spot beside her. 「Come over here.」 「Why?」 「Because it tastes better when you eat it closer.」 「Pudding tastes the same no matter where you eat it.」 「You think so? It'll taste better, so just try it.」 Sendai-san said with a grin, eating her pudding. There was no reason to do what she said. I'd never heard of pudding changing flavor based on where you ate it, and she was just making up half-baked excuses. She was definitely planning to do something weird once I sat next to her, or maybe even try to eat my pudding. That was why I didn't need to sit next to her, but since I'd gotten to eat a good meal today thanks to Sendai-san, I figured I could let her fool me just this once. 「I guess I'll try it.」 I sat down beside her and took a bite of pudding. As expected, the taste didn't change. 「Is it good?」 「It's good, but it's the same as before.」 「I see. Want a taste of mine?」 Sendai-san started scooping up some pudding with her spoon, so I pushed her arm away. 「I'm not eating it,」 I declared. 「But it's good.」 I heard her mutter to herself beside me, but she was eating the same pudding as me, so there was no point in having one bite or two. No matter how much she ate, it would taste the same. 「Then, can I take a picture of you? The last Miyagi of the year?」 Sendai-san set her pudding down on the table, pulled out her phone, and aimed it at me. 「Absolutely not.」 「You're so stingy, Miyagi.」 「I'm fine with being stingy.」 「Then let me have a bite of your pudding.」 「It tastes the same, so just eat your own.」 「Fine, I will.」 Sendai-san gave up surprisingly easily and picked up the pudding she'd set on the table. Then she scooped up one bite, then another, and ate them. 「Hey, Miyagi.」 Sendai-san said quietly, dropping her gaze to the pudding that was now two-thirds gone. 「What?」 「Don't let Mio or my upperclassman call you Shiori.」 「I have no intention of letting them.」 「If you do, I'll start calling you Shiori too.」 She whispered the words directly into my ear, and I instinctively shoved her shoulder. 「Miyagi, that's dangerous. I almost dropped my pudding.」 Her voice felt good. It made me remember things I didn't need to remember. 「That's because you suddenly got so close, Sendai-san. It's hard to eat my pudding like this, so back off.」 I scooped up some pudding to cover it up and brought the spoon to my mouth.
